sentence: This project provides imaging and image-guided therapy tools that support preclinical cancer research in animal models.
This project uses artificial intelligence on abdominal CT scans to study hepatic steatosis in people with and without HIV infection.
This project uses a digital clock drawing test, machine learning and neuroimaging to find early changes of Alzheimer's disease.
This project gives researchers genetic, genomic and metabolomic tools to study the molecular pathways behind nutrition and obesity.
This project studies the pathways of a key regulator of plasma lipoprotein metabolism to understand how lipid homeostasis is maintained.
This project tries to find out how acute myeloid leukemia tumor cells develop resistance to drugs.
This project provides tick cell lines and tools, and studies how tick cells respond to infection by tick-borne pathogens.
This project studies how chikungunya virus and Aedes mosquitoes evolve together, using experimental evolution and functional genetic approaches.
This project studies brain tumor biology to find more effective and targeted treatments.
This project tests why some urothelial cancer patients respond to combined antibody-drug conjugate and immunotherapy, using patient samples and bladder cancer mouse models.
This project uses structural insights on membrane-related components of HIV to design immunogens for a vaccine that induces effective immune responses.
This project builds a gut-on-a-chip from canine patient intestinal organoids to study how the gut microbiome affects inflammatory bowel disease.
This project studies endometrial regeneration and stem cells in the endometrium to understand endometriosis.
This project provides sequencing and computing tools that help researchers study genes and microbes in cystic fibrosis.
This project provides small molecule screening, imaging and histology equipment to help discover and develop treatments for human pathogens.
This project studies how brain-derived neurotrophic factor controls genes that shape the maturation of inhibition in the mouse visual cortex.
This project studies how skeletal muscle and heart keep their mitochondria healthy under lipid-induced bioenergetic stress.
This project develops nanowired, hypoimmunogenic cardiac organoids to use as an off-the-shelf therapy for heart repair.
This project designs and tests mobility devices, robots and other systems for veterans with disabilities.
This project shows how laboratory mice can be used to study hearing and balance disorders.
